name: Pelso Mango-Habanero Caramel Pulls
description: Long-pull synth-caramel chews with a slow mango sweetness that builds into a genuine habanero finish. Each piece is individually wrapped in heat-stamped foil printed with rotating neighborhood tags.
flavor_profile: Initial rich caramel and ripe mango; mid-chew tropical sweetness; lingering dry habanero heat that sits at the back of the throat for two to three minutes
cultural_context: A staple in Shelf corner shops and Tier 2 transit kiosks. The rotating neighborhood tag foil makes them a minor collector item — kids trade wrappers with tags from districts they've never visited. Older buyers buy them for the heat.
story_hooks: A runner uses the distinctive foil wrappers as dead-drop markers — a specific neighborhood tag left on a specific bench means a message is waiting
Pelso's founder is being pressured by a corponation to sell the recipe; she'd rather burn the factory
A batch contaminated with an unlicensed stimulant compound is circulating — the heat is masking the taste difference
